segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It's for people who visit the exhibition to read, and I'm absolutely certain they will.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It explains the reasons behind our work, and they'll want to know what it all means.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: We've got a strict word limit to stick to.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: But I've got so much to say.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It won't be easy to say it in so few words.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Hmm.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So what about other organizational stuff?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: We'll need good lighting, for one thing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The technical guys are doing that, aren't they?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: One thing to do is copy a load of comment forms so people can write what they think of the exhibition.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Hopefully they'll be kind.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: I'm sure they will.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: I don't know about the journalists who've been invited, though.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: They might not be quite as nice to us.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Well, fingers crossed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: You never know.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30 on page six.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Now listen and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So our tutor suggested visiting a few exhibitions to look at the way work is presented and to give us a few ideas about improving and displaying our own work.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Yeah, I liked the On the Water exhibition.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The way the artist used the brush strokes in the oil painting to create a sense of movement was amazing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Hmm.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: It takes a long time to develop skill like that.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Maybe we'll get there one day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: What I liked about the City Life exhibition was the fact that although the paintings themselves were of busy places, the display itself wasn't crowded at all.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Perhaps the fact that the paintings were actually quite small was what created a more open feeling to the exhibition.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Though the way they were arranged wasn't especially unusual.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: And then there was the Faces exhibition.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: I mean.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Painting people's portraits isn't a new thing, but what I did like was the way the artist managed to reproduce the exact tones of the skin and hair of the people in the pictures.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: And the last exhibition we went to see was moods.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Mm hmm.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: I expected that to show emotions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: People laughing, crying, whatever.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: But it was about plants.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: You don't tend to think of trees and flowers having feelings.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: And I'm not sure they do.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: But it certainly seemed that way in the pictures.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Not the most obvious choice of subject, that's for sure.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Anyway, I guess we'd better get on with it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: That is the end of Section three.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Now turn to section four on page seven.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Section four.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You will hear part of a student presentation about a conservation project on the Florida coast of the United States.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: First you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40 on page seven.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Today, I'm going to be talking about the first year of a regeneration project in a mangrove forest.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Mangrove forests are found along river estuaries and coastlines and are important because they prevent flooding by acting as a barrier between the land and sea.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The mangrove trees have special roots which can breathe and allow them to survive in thick, airless mud.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: They are also a very important habitat for wading birds, fish and other animals in the area where the project is taking place.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: There have been a number of problems since the area was first settled over 100 years ago.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Many of the mangrove trees were initially burnt as firewood by local farmers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The mangrove forests were also poisoned by settlers farming methods because the farmers used fertilizer to increase crop yields.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: And this started to seep into the water, eventually killing part of the mangrove forest.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Farming in the area wasn't successful, and what was left of the mangrove forest area wasn't valued by local people as crops couldn't be grown there.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: And so what happened was that the area started to be used as somewhere to dump trash.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Action was urgently needed to protect the mangrove forest and prevent flooding.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: And so the mangrove regeneration project was set up.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The conservationists involved decided to construct a sand barrier around the forests, but unfortunately this proved to be ineffective.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The only way forward appeared to be to grow new mangroves from seed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Several species of mangrove inhabit the forests in this area of the United States.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: But it is the gray mangroves that we are concerned with here.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The seed of this plant is about the size of an almond, and most seeds fall only when they are fully ripe.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The Mangrove Regeneration Project first began three years ago.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The first set of seedlings was planted in small plots and left to germinate in a hothouse.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The plants thrived and large roots appeared at the bottom of the pots.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Ideally, these seedlings should have been conditioned with increasingly salty water before being planted in the sea.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: They had, in fact only been watered with rainwater as the plants weren't used to a saline environment.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: It was decided to plant them out on the south side of a small island nearby.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: It was hoped that this would allow them to get used to salt water gradually.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Since this part of the island was flooded every day at high tide, there were over 100 plants planted in this particular spot, and it was necessary to protect them not from the large number of wading birds which visit the area looking for food, but from the large rabbit colony living in the area.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The process for the second set of seedlings was completely different.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Young seedlings were collected from the forests and then taken to a new site.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The seedlings were then planted in the seabed behind old mangrove roots for protection.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: However, this method did not prove very successful, and the vast majority of these seedlings were washed away in a storm.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Luckily, the first set of seedlings survived, and this method is the one which the project will continue to use in the future.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Now I'd like to describe in more detail the process.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: That is the end of Section four.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You now have half a minute to check your answers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: That is the end of the listening test.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You now have 10 minutes to transfer your answers to the listening answer sheet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You have 2 minutes left.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You have one minute left.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Please stop writing and wait for your question booklet to be collected.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You will hear a talk about the island of New Guinea and some of the people of Papua New Guinea.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 10.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Today's talk is about the fascinating culture of New Guinea, an island divided in two politically, but with huge diversity in both parts.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: For those of you who don't know, New Guinea is located in Oceania in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, north of Australia.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Since 1975, the eastern side has been the independent country of Papua New Guinea, while the western side consists of the Indonesian administered provinces of Papua and West Papua.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Papua New Guinea has 7 million inhabitants and is an incredibly rural country with only 18% of the population living in urban areas.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It has 852 known languages and is one of the least explored terrains on the planet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now, one of the reasons that Papua New Guinea and indeed the whole of New Guinea is such an interesting place is that it's home to hundreds of traditional tribes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Perhaps better described as distinct social groups, each one numbering hundreds or even thousands of members.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: In the Indonesian part of New Guinea, that is the provinces of Papua and West Papua.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: There are 312 different tribes, including around 44 uncontacted ones.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: These are tribes who up until now hadn't had any contact with the outside world, even with other neighboring tribes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Of course, everyone is most curious to know about these tribes, but by definition we have little or no information on them.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I'm now going to talk about the tribes of the Papua New Guinea highlands.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: These people only rarely had contact with the outside world until the 1960s, so they are still relatively isolated.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: When we start to examine the tribes, we see a common theme, which is the use of various methods to intimidate other groups so as to protect their own tribe.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Let's look first at the Huli wig men, a tribe of about 14,000 from the Tari highlands of Papua New Guinea.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: They have given their faces a very distinctive look by using yellow paint and they wear belts made of pigtails, aprons made of leaves and wigs, which are a sort of hat made from their own hair.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This look is designed to scare off outsiders, which they also do with their bird dances, which mimic the birds of paradise that inhabit their land.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Another Highland tribe, the Asaro mud men, have the same intention as the Huli Wickman to ward off outsiders by smearing themselves in clay and mud.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: They adopt the form of the river spirits, which are known to terrify their enemies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Their elaborate appearances further supplemented with extended fingernails.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And they wear terrifying masks which serve to accentuate their ferocious look.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The Asaro mud men were discovered by the outside world less than 80 years ago, but have now become a symbol of Papua New Guinea and make an important contribution to the tourist trade.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: A third tribe that has become well-known is the timber who live high in the mountains.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The chimp boo skeleton dancers used to dance to intimidate their enemies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This tribe traditionally lived in male, female segregated houses, though they are now increasingly living in family groups.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This group, to now display their traditional dances, not to scare off other tribes, but more to entertain tourists.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: An interesting event, the Mount Hagen Sing Sing takes place every year involving over 50 tribes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This came about due to the constant fighting between tribes, which became a serious problem for the Papua New Guinea government.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So in 1961 it came up with the idea of a cultural show which would bring together as many tribes as possible in peace and pride in their cultural heritage.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The Mount Hagen Sing Sing is a wonderful opportunity for Papua New Guinea to showcase its fascinating cultural heritage at this event.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Tourists and locals alike can witness the spectacular costumes, including six feet high headdresses made of flowers, shells and feathers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Inevitably, there is some loss of authenticity associated with this kind of event.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: For example, chemical dyes are now used instead of the natural ones the tribes used earlier.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: However, a poor developing country has to exploit whatever resources it has, and the wealth of this region is its tribal peoples.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Part two, you will hear a talk between a radio host and a college student called Darren Almond about how to improve photography skills.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Good afternoon, our beloved listeners.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Welcome to today's Capturing the Moment program.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Today, we have Darren Almond here with us.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: He is a college student who has just won an award for his set of shots of red squirrels.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Welcome, Daryn.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now, can you tell us a bit about this lovely creature and how you managed to take such wonderful photos?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Well, the red squirrel is Britain's only native squirrel.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's graceful and athletic.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Its Latin name, Sirus Vulgaris, comes from the Greek words describing a common type of animal which sits in the shadow of its own tail.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: At first I thought this description was funny and was kind of an exaggeration, but now I realize that this name suits them very well.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Their fluffy tails under the sun normally cast a big shadow over themselves.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You will be lucky to see a red squirrel in the areas where they still survive due to its timid nature and decreasing number in the wild.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In the late 1800s, when gray squirrels and exotic species were first introduced into Britain, there were only about 20,000 red squirrels left, the majority of which lived in the north of England.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The grays carry a disease called the squirrel pox virus, which could lead to the deaths of red squirrels.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: But their number had already declined before the disease spread there.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The shrinking population actually corresponds to decreases in the number of nuts available.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The Red Squirrels Primary Food Source.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I accidentally left some nuts in my garden one day and I found that they had been eaten the next morning.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It could have been rats as they have a very similar food category to red squirrels.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: But I knew it was red squirrels because of their different feeding habits.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Rats bite a hole in the nuts, whereas red squirrels crack the nuts in half and eat the kernels.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: After a week or so, the red squirrels became regular visitors to my garden, making them ideal subjects for my photography project.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Unfortunately, I had to shoot only in my garden, partly because I couldn't find another spot to cite red squirrels on a regular basis.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Also, this could block out any outside distractions, and I could focus solely on my subject during the shooting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Other animals, like birds, got caught in the frame together sometimes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I'm more than satisfied with my photos, even though I only practiced a few times and used just a second hand camera from my friend.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: My great mentor helped me with the shooting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I got great tutorials from him and was able to shoot better photos.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now listen and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Thank you, Daryn.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The award winning photos will be on display in a local museum for the coming month.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We're looking forward to the exhibition.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So tell us about the award.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I sent my portfolio for the competition hosted by a national newspaper.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I wasn't expecting the third prize, so when they notified me of the result on the phone, I was really excited.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Do you have some tips for our audience to help improve their photography skills?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Of course.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Here are three things I think photographers can work on to get a better shot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: First of all, good composition is key to a lovely shot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Normally an image is center of interest, is placed at one of the intersections that transact the whole picture in order to achieve balance.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: A secondary object, so to speak, can be added to the scene at the opposing intersection.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So, for instance, in one of my shots, a red squirrel at the top left is staring at a nut at the lower right corner.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: This is called the rule of thirds.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Lighting is another essential element if you want to be rewarded with a superb photo.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The direction of the light falling on your subject is most important of all.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: You need to look at your subject carefully and watch how the shadows fall.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: If you're able to choose the time of day to shoot your pictures, lighting is most ideal in the late afternoon.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Try to position yourself so that the sun hits your subject from the side.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: This helps create a 3-D effect in the picture to further improve on your photography skills.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It is advised to take detailed notes of timing, position, weather, etc..

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: By doing so, it's easier to review and adjust accordingly.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And there is always room for improvement.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That is the end of part two.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Part three, you will hear two students called Aria and John discussing the research on water hyacinths.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: John, how is it going with your research on water hyacinth?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Well, I went on a field trip on my own and collected the primary data after I came back.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I also referred to the published data.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So what do you know about this plant?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The water hyacinth grows in tropical countries.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: It has beautiful purple blue flowers, but everybody hates it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Why is that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The water hyacinth, as the world's worst invasive aquatic plant has attracted significant attention.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Millions of these plants grow in rivers and lakes and are brought huge environmental and cultural problems to the local people.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Farmers cannot travel in boats on the water and thus cannot fish in it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: In addition, heavy free floating mats of water hyacinth are clogging the dam at the power station West Africa.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Turbines of the power station are often shut down because of the intertwined leaves.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Dams often cease to function as a result, severely restricting the electricity generation.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Dense mats of water hyacinth also shade the surface and prevent algae growth, thus limiting the production of oxygen and threatening the survival of fish.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So where did Water Hyacinth originate from?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The water hyacinth is native to the Amazon basin in Latin America.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: It is spread mainly to the tropics and subtropics from much of the world since the 1800s.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Later, it was introduced into Europe and Africa as an ornamental garden pond plant due to its beauty.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Flowers of this plant were being sold in local markets and African countries as a source of income for women since the 1900s.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: This weed has infested lakes, rivers and creeks of the delta areas in West Africa.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I guess whoever introduced this plant had never expected the disastrous impact it would have on the local ecological environment.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: What kind of habitat does water hyacinth thrive most in?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Well, it has been discovered that the nutrient rich environment contribute significantly to the rapid proliferation of this weed, which obtains its nutrients directly from the water.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: This is normally compounded with a decrease of nutrients along the river banks.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Why is that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The main reason for soil nutrient loss is that local residents cut down trees.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Excessive deforestation accelerates soil erosion, which indirectly compound this issue.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Without enough trees to retain nutrients in the soil, frequent rain might partly aggravate this by carrying some of the nutrients into the waterways.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Are there any effective measures to control or even eradicate this weed?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: A number of approaches have been widely applied throughout the world.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Among them, biological control, is the most widely favored long term control method by introducing a type of insects that feeds on the water hyacinth.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So far, Nigeria has used this method for six months.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: However, water hyacinth won't be removed and immediately the side effects of this method on local ecology will remain unforeseen for years because it takes time for this external insect species to reach a density sufficient enough to affect ecological development.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Then what about other approaches?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Is there a quicker way to control it?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Well, the mechanical removal of water hyacinth is seen as the best short term solution.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: This option includes harvesting plants and inside cutting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: This method can immediately open physical space for fish and boat traffic.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: It is, however, inefficient for workers to process extensive areas and costly to use large cutting and dredging equipment.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Ironically, it cost even more to dispose of this plant than to remove it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now listen and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Can we make use of this weed and turn it into something good?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Now scientists think that water hyacinth can be useful.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The plant itself, although more than 95% water, has a fibrous tissue and a high energy and protein content and can be used for a variety of useful applications.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So what do people do with water hyacinth that is initially removed?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: First, the cut down water hyacinth is left to dry under the sun for a few days before being mixed with ash and animal manure.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The mixture can be used as alternative soil rather than fertilizer.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: It can grow crops with increased yield.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That sounds interesting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Mushroom farmers can benefit from water hyacinth as well, using the mixture mentioned earlier.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Mushrooms generally grow much faster so that farmers can harvest mushrooms sooner, which enables them to make money faster.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I see it can be used to grow oyster and straw mushrooms, right?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: In India, attempts have been made to grow the types of edible mushrooms organically utilizing water hyacinth.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: These mushrooms provide sufficient nutritional values, including minerals and high quality protein, which are essential to people's level of fitness.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Right.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Are there any other measures taken to utilize water hyacinth.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: In South East Asia?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: People feed cows using chopped water hyacinth mixed with other vegetables.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Then the waste from the cows is treated to produce methane gas, which can be used as fuel for cooking, lighting or powering an engine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And with global warming getting worse, developing alternative source of energy will be more urgent than ever.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Maybe in the future people will love water hyacinth instead of hating it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Yes, that's very likely if we can make full use of this weed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That is the end of part three.

segments.text: Part four, you will hear part of a lecture on nanotechnology and its applications.

segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Today's lecture is the first of a series of lectures on nanotechnology.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Nanotechnology, sometimes shortened to nanotech, refers to the manipulation of matter on an atomic and molecular level.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's the science, engineering and technology conducted at the nanoscale, which is about 1 to 100 nano meters.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It is the study and application of extremely small things and can be used across all the other science fields.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Just how small is that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: A nano meter is one billionth of a meter.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The idea of nanoscale research first started from a physicist called Richard Feynman in 1959.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: He envisaged a process in which scientists would be able to manipulate and control individual atoms and molecules.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In fact, it wasn't until 1981, with the invention of a special kind of microscope that modern nanotechnology truly began.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Even though nanotechnology has created many new materials and devices with a vast range of applications, there is always concern over these are natural products.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Many people are worried that they may pose a threat to the environment, health and safety, also known as VHS.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In order to better understand and evaluate the potential harm, risk assessment has been introduced.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There are also ongoing international collaborations on the Nano s research and related policy issues.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Despite the concern, nanotechnology has benefited society in unexpected ways in the food processing industry.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Nanotechnology is leveraged against iron deficiency, which triggers anemia, for example, by reducing the particle size in potatoes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: This new technology improves the bioavailability of this nutritional ingredient without the tendency to cause color and odor changes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In terms of packaging, nanomaterials are more economical and are used in all sorts of products.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Chocolate in particular.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Nanotechnology can also enhance the flavor of food.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: On a domestic scale, we expect more smart furniture, which is made of shape, memory alloys to be manufactured.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: But nanotechnology has much wider application than this and could also help develop sustainable agriculture.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It offers great potential to strengthen the effect of fertilizers, thereby minimizing the environmental impact and boosting the productivity of plants in the soil.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In the area of medicine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Bioengineers have developed simple and inexpensive nanoscale delivery vehicles.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Conductors like carbon nanotubes have been invented with varying structures.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Such nanotubes have become increasingly attractive to researchers because of their ability to efficiently deliver drugs into veins.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: This means that higher doses of drugs loaded on them can be transported from the administration sites to the effects related sites such as cancer focuses, thus decreasing toxic side effects while increasing the treatment effects.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The research team has also developed a widely accepted material that can be used to coat different surfaces, including wood, plastic and glass.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It is mainly comprised of silver.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Such nanoparticles can eventually kill some microbes due to the antiseptic properties.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The whole process is simple, easy to apply, and, more importantly, harmless to the environment.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Surprisingly, nanotechnology has major implications for our health as well by changing the metabolic rate through a particular type of protein.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Obese patients are able to burn calories faster, even under a high calorie diet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Therefore, treatment programs are provided for patients to lose weight by disposing of excess fat in a relatively safer manner.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The finding may help explain why overweight people struggle to lose weight.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Their stored fat is actively fighting against their efforts to burn it off at the molecular level.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Further research is mainly focused on the clinical and commercial developments of therapies for obesity, diabetes and other associated conditions such as heart disease.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In terms of cosmetics, the applications of nanotechnology and nanomaterials can be found in many products.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: There are two main uses for nanotechnology in cosmetics.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The first one is that nanoparticles are commonly used as UV filters in anti-aging suncare products to avoid skin damage caused by the sun.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In addition, nanotechnology has played an important role in delivering active ingredients to the skin.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The mechanism proves to improve the bioavailability of actives and enhance skin hydration.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The wide variety of nanotechnology applications leave no doubt that this field will only continue to get more exciting, and I look forward to seeing these developments further branch out.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That is the end of part four.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Today's talk is about the fascinating culture of New Guinea, an island divided in two politically, but with huge diversity in both parts.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: For those of you who don't know, New Guinea is located in Oceania in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, north of Australia.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Since 1975, the eastern side has been the independent country of Papua New Guinea, while the western side consists of the Indonesian administered provinces of Papua and West Papua.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Papua New Guinea has 7 million inhabitants and is an incredibly rural country with only 18% of the population living in urban areas.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: It has 852 known languages and is one of the least explored terrains on the planet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Now, one of the reasons that Papua New Guinea and indeed the whole of New Guinea is such an interesting place is that it's home to hundreds of traditional tribes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Perhaps better described as distinct social groups, each one numbering hundreds or even thousands of members.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: In the Indonesian part of New Guinea, that is the provinces of Papua and West Papua.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: There are 312 different tribes, including around 44 uncontacted ones.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: These are tribes who up until now hadn't had any contact with the outside world, even with other neighboring tribes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Of course, everyone is most curious to know about these tribes, but by definition we have little or no information on them.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: I'm now going to talk about the tribes of the Papua New Guinea highlands.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: These people only rarely had contact with the outside world until the 1960s, so they are still relatively isolated.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: When we start to examine the tribes, we see a common theme, which is the use of various methods to intimidate other groups so as to protect their own tribe.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Let's look first at the Huli wig men, a tribe of about 14,000 from the Tari highlands of Papua New Guinea.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: They have given their faces a very distinctive look by using yellow paint and they wear belts made of pigtails, aprons made of leaves and wigs, which are a sort of hat made from their own hair.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: This look is designed to scare off outsiders, which they also do with their bird dances, which mimic the birds of paradise that inhabit their land.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Another Highland tribe, the Asaro mud men, have the same intention as the Huli Wickman to ward off outsiders by smearing themselves in clay and mud.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: They adopt the form of the river spirits, which are known to terrify their enemies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Their elaborate appearances further supplemented with extended fingernails.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: And they wear terrifying masks which serve to accentuate their ferocious look.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The Asaro mud men were discovered by the outside world less than 80 years ago, but have now become a symbol of Papua New Guinea and make an important contribution to the tourist trade.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: A third tribe that has become well-known is the timber who live high in the mountains.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The chimp boo skeleton dancers used to dance to intimidate their enemies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: This tribe traditionally lived in male, female segregated houses, though they are now increasingly living in family groups.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: This group, to now display their traditional dances, not to scare off other tribes, but more to entertain tourists.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: An interesting event, the Mount Hagen Sing Sing takes place every year involving over 50 tribes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: This came about due to the constant fighting between tribes, which became a serious problem for the Papua New Guinea government.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: So in 1961 it came up with the idea of a cultural show which would bring together as many tribes as possible in peace and pride in their cultural heritage.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The Mount Hagen Sing Sing is a wonderful opportunity for Papua New Guinea to showcase its fascinating cultural heritage at this event.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Tourists and locals alike can witness the spectacular costumes, including six feet high headdresses made of flowers, shells and feathers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Inevitably, there is some loss of authenticity associated with this kind of event.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: For example, chemical dyes are now used instead of the natural ones the tribes used earlier.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: However, a poor developing country has to exploit whatever resources it has, and the wealth of this region is its tribal peoples.

segments.transcript: Well, the red squirrel is Britain's only native squirrel.

segments.transcript: It's graceful and athletic.

segments.transcript: Its Latin name, Sirus Vulgaris, comes from the Greek words describing a common type of animal which sits in the shadow of its own tail.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: At first I thought this description was funny and was kind of an exaggeration, but now I realize that this name suits them very well.

segments.transcript: Their fluffy tails under the sun normally cast a big shadow over themselves.

segments.transcript: But their number had already declined before the disease spread there.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The shrinking population actually corresponds to decreases in the number of nuts available.

segments.transcript: The Red Squirrels Primary Food Source.

segments.transcript: I accidentally left some nuts in my garden one day and I found that they had been eaten the next morning.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: But I knew it was red squirrels because of their different feeding habits.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Rats bite a hole in the nuts, whereas red squirrels crack the nuts in half and eat the kernels.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: After a week or so, the red squirrels became regular visitors to my garden, making them ideal subjects for my photography project.

segments.transcript: Do you have some tips for our audience to help improve their photography skills?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Of course.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Here are three things I think photographers can work on to get a better shot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: First of all, good composition is key to a lovely shot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Normally an image is center of interest, is placed at one of the intersections that transact the whole picture in order to achieve balance.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: A secondary object, so to speak, can be added to the scene at the opposing intersection.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: So, for instance, in one of my shots, a red squirrel at the top left is staring at a nut at the lower right corner.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: This is called the rule of thirds.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Lighting is another essential element if you want to be rewarded with a superb photo.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The direction of the light falling on your subject is most important of all.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: You need to look at your subject carefully and watch how the shadows fall.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: If you're able to choose the time of day to shoot your pictures, lighting is most ideal in the late afternoon.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Try to position yourself so that the sun hits your subject from the side.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: This helps create a 3-D effect in the picture to further improve on your photography skills.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It is advised to take detailed notes of timing, position, weather, etc..

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: By doing so, it's easier to review and adjust accordingly.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: And there is always room for improvement.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Without enough trees to retain nutrients in the soil, frequent rain might partly aggravate this by carrying some of the nutrients into the waterways.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Are there any effective measures to control or even eradicate this weed?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Yes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: A number of approaches have been widely applied throughout the world.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Among them, biological control, is the most widely favored long term control method by introducing a type of insects that feeds on the water hyacinth.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: So far, Nigeria has used this method for six months.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: However, water hyacinth won't be removed and immediately the side effects of this method on local ecology will remain unforeseen for years because it takes time for this external insect species to reach a density sufficient enough to affect ecological development.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Then what about other approaches?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Is there a quicker way to control it?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Well, the mechanical removal of water hyacinth is seen as the best short term solution.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: This option includes harvesting plants and inside cutting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: This method can immediately open physical space for fish and boat traffic.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: It is, however, inefficient for workers to process extensive areas and costly to use large cutting and dredging equipment.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Ironically, it cost even more to dispose of this plant than to remove it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Now listen and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Can we make use of this weed and turn it into something good?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Now scientists think that water hyacinth can be useful.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: The plant itself, although more than 95% water, has a fibrous tissue and a high energy and protein content and can be used for a variety of useful applications.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So what do people do with water hyacinth that is initially removed?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: First, the cut down water hyacinth is left to dry under the sun for a few days before being mixed with ash and animal manure.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: The mixture can be used as alternative soil rather than fertilizer.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: It can grow crops with increased yield.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: That sounds interesting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Mushroom farmers can benefit from water hyacinth as well, using the mixture mentioned earlier.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Mushrooms generally grow much faster so that farmers can harvest mushrooms sooner, which enables them to make money faster.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: I see it can be used to grow oyster and straw mushrooms, right?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Yes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: In India, attempts have been made to grow the types of edible mushrooms organically utilizing water hyacinth.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: These mushrooms provide sufficient nutritional values, including minerals and high quality protein, which are essential to people's level of fitness.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Right.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Are there any other measures taken to utilize water hyacinth.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: In South East Asia?

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: People feed cows using chopped water hyacinth mixed with other vegetables.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Then the waste from the cows is treated to produce methane gas, which can be used as fuel for cooking, lighting or powering an engine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: And with global warming getting worse, developing alternative source of energy will be more urgent than ever.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Maybe in the future people will love water hyacinth instead of hating it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.transcript: Yes, that's very likely if we can make full use of this weed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: That is the end of part three.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Part four, you will hear part of a lecture on nanotechnology and its applications.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: First, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Today's lecture is the first of a series of lectures on nanotechnology.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Nanotechnology, sometimes shortened to nanotech, refers to the manipulation of matter on an atomic and molecular level.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It's the science, engineering and technology conducted at the nanoscale, which is about 1 to 100 nano meters.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It is the study and application of extremely small things and can be used across all the other science fields.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Just how small is that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: A nano meter is one billionth of a meter.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The idea of nanoscale research first started from a physicist called Richard Feynman in 1959.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: He envisaged a process in which scientists would be able to manipulate and control individual atoms and molecules.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: In fact, it wasn't until 1981, with the invention of a special kind of microscope that modern nanotechnology truly began.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Even though nanotechnology has created many new materials and devices with a vast range of applications, there is always concern over these are natural products.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Many people are worried that they may pose a threat to the environment, health and safety, also known as VHS.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: In order to better understand and evaluate the potential harm, risk assessment has been introduced.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: There are also ongoing international collaborations on the Nano s research and related policy issues.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Despite the concern, nanotechnology has benefited society in unexpected ways in the food processing industry.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Nanotechnology is leveraged against iron deficiency, which triggers anemia, for example, by reducing the particle size in potatoes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: This new technology improves the bioavailability of this nutritional ingredient without the tendency to cause color and odor changes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: In terms of packaging, nanomaterials are more economical and are used in all sorts of products.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Chocolate in particular.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Nanotechnology can also enhance the flavor of food.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: On a domestic scale, we expect more smart furniture, which is made of shape, memory alloys to be manufactured.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: But nanotechnology has much wider application than this and could also help develop sustainable agriculture.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It offers great potential to strengthen the effect of fertilizers, thereby minimizing the environmental impact and boosting the productivity of plants in the soil.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: In the area of medicine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Bioengineers have developed simple and inexpensive nanoscale delivery vehicles.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Conductors like carbon nanotubes have been invented with varying structures.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Such nanotubes have become increasingly attractive to researchers because of their ability to efficiently deliver drugs into veins.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: This means that higher doses of drugs loaded on them can be transported from the administration sites to the effects related sites such as cancer focuses, thus decreasing toxic side effects while increasing the treatment effects.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The research team has also developed a widely accepted material that can be used to coat different surfaces, including wood, plastic and glass.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: It is mainly comprised of silver.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Such nanoparticles can eventually kill some microbes due to the antiseptic properties.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The whole process is simple, easy to apply, and, more importantly, harmless to the environment.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Surprisingly, nanotechnology has major implications for our health as well by changing the metabolic rate through a particular type of protein.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Obese patients are able to burn calories faster, even under a high calorie diet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Therefore, treatment programs are provided for patients to lose weight by disposing of excess fat in a relatively safer manner.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The finding may help explain why overweight people struggle to lose weight.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Their stored fat is actively fighting against their efforts to burn it off at the molecular level.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: Further research is mainly focused on the clinical and commercial developments of therapies for obesity, diabetes and other associated conditions such as heart disease.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: In terms of cosmetics, the applications of nanotechnology and nanomaterials can be found in many products.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: There are two main uses for nanotechnology in cosmetics.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The first one is that nanoparticles are commonly used as UV filters in anti-aging suncare products to avoid skin damage caused by the sun.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: In addition, nanotechnology has played an important role in delivering active ingredients to the skin.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The mechanism proves to improve the bioavailability of actives and enhance skin hydration.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.transcript: The wide variety of nanotechnology applications leave no doubt that this field will only continue to get more exciting, and I look forward to seeing these developments further branch out.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: That is the end of part four.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: You now have one minute to check your answers to part four.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This is the third session of the series of lectures on wildlife.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: For this lecture, we're going to look at two studies on the habitats of birds and protection measures taken in Australia, including the basic methodology and related areas of research.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now let me give you some background information about the first research project on birds.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The study was carried out by R.B.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Cunningham and his team from the Australian National University in 1995.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The primary goal was to detect the breeding habits and resting sites of some birds, especially those protected species in urban regions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: These species included birds like peregrine falcons and kestrels in Australia.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The bird dataset consisted of a total of 153 species recorded from 946 sites.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: One might expect that in order to obtain valid data on their distribution patterns and population densities, researchers had to count through binoculars.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Instead, they managed to estimate with various standard distance sampling methods, like random sampling.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In addition, a mapping system was used to study their companionship behaviour.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It recorded proposed birds nesting sites to monitor the mating behaviour of targeted species to obtain valid data of birds whereabouts.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Researchers attached identity tags to birds legs, transmitting radio signals.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The tagging process was done when the birds were between five and seven days of age.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: After the initial tagging data was collected from subsets of radio tagged birds, making it possible to assess the trends of birds over 15 months.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So what did they find?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Well, as it turned out, many of the birds tagged had the tendency to nest in the same habitats where they grew up.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Their nesting sites were quite varied and included freshwater reed beds, tidal reed beds, agricultural crops and manmade sites.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Even though naturally occurring nests were common, birds, sometimes accidentally nested in manmade devices like power towers, chimneys and tunnels.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This research also studied the impact of humans on bird communities and found out that pollution had contributed greatly to the declining birth rates of some species which were considered to be extinct or threatened to vanish from the study area.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: These species are dependent on natural forests because of their breeding holes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They will become extinct when local natural forests continue to be polluted heavily.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A number of measures were thus taken by members from local animal conservation organisations to boost their alarming survival rates.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Firstly, breeding boxes were placed in trees, taking on the role of breeding holes that were contaminated.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Protection guidelines were also introduced strictly prohibiting killing, disturbance and habitat destruction.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A further measure was taken to ensure the safety of birds from wind farms.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In fact, birds are sometimes shaded by wind turbine blades.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A great deal of work was done on how to prevent them from colliding with turbines.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A case in point was protecting space for bird migration by ensuring that migratory routes were kept free.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Falcons generally cope well with wind turbines, but not in weather conditions where visibility is bad.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So with knowledge of how fast falcons fly, bird stations in northern Australia can notify wind farms further south of the Falcons approach so that turbines can be shut down as they pass by.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Then another piece of research was done a couple of years later by Conway in 2006.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: His team detected the calling frequency of seabirds flying at night.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Acoustic signals are important communication tools for birds.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: These signals can indicate social cohesion, prey, location and breeding behaviour.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Courtship songs are common amongst various species during mating seasons.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Males produce calling songs that attract distant females, and then courtship songs will induce nearby females to respond.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Surveyors also took recordings of the sounds of all the individual birds detected.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A tablet PC was used to process detailed information like sound pitch, spectrum, length and timing of surveys to minimise the disturbance on the bird community.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: All the sounds were recorded from a distance, using microphones to detect noise.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They found that the probability of call events was much higher for solitary birds communicating early and late in the day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Further analysis indicated that during foraging, the frequency of calls was significantly greater for birds encountering schooling, fish and birds called sooner after a catch in these foraging scenarios compared with when only single fish were encountered.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The results of this study showed that increased calling activity in the presence of more profitable prey could be of crucial importance to seabirds that benefit from group foraging.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three. ------------------------------------------------ Part four, you will hear part of a lecture on bird research in Australia.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: First you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Good afternoon.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: This is the third session of the series of lectures on wildlife.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: For this lecture, we're going to look at two studies on the habitats of birds and protection measures taken in Australia, including the basic methodology and related areas of research.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Now let me give you some background information about the first research project on birds.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The study was carried out by R.B.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Cunningham and his team from the Australian National University in 1995.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The primary goal was to detect the breeding habits and resting sites of some birds, especially those protected species in urban regions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: These species included birds like peregrine falcons and kestrels in Australia.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The bird dataset consisted of a total of 153 species recorded from 946 sites.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: One might expect that in order to obtain valid data on their distribution patterns and population densities, researchers had to count through binoculars.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Instead, they managed to estimate with various standard distance sampling methods, like random sampling.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: In addition, a mapping system was used to study their companionship behaviour.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: It recorded proposed birds nesting sites to monitor the mating behaviour of targeted species to obtain valid data of birds whereabouts.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Researchers attached identity tags to birds legs, transmitting radio signals.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The tagging process was done when the birds were between five and seven days of age.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: After the initial tagging data was collected from subsets of radio tagged birds, making it possible to assess the trends of birds over 15 months.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So what did they find?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Well, as it turned out, many of the birds tagged had the tendency to nest in the same habitats where they grew up.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Their nesting sites were quite varied and included freshwater reed beds, tidal reed beds, agricultural crops and manmade sites.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Even though naturally occurring nests were common, birds, sometimes accidentally nested in manmade devices like power towers, chimneys and tunnels.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: This research also studied the impact of humans on bird communities and found out that pollution had contributed greatly to the declining birth rates of some species which were considered to be extinct or threatened to vanish from the study area.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: These species are dependent on natural forests because of their breeding holes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: They will become extinct when local natural forests continue to be polluted heavily.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A number of measures were thus taken by members from local animal conservation organisations to boost their alarming survival rates.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Firstly, breeding boxes were placed in trees, taking on the role of breeding holes that were contaminated.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Protection guidelines were also introduced strictly prohibiting killing, disturbance and habitat destruction.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A further measure was taken to ensure the safety of birds from wind farms.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: In fact, birds are sometimes shaded by wind turbine blades.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A great deal of work was done on how to prevent them from colliding with turbines.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A case in point was protecting space for bird migration by ensuring that migratory routes were kept free.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Falcons generally cope well with wind turbines, but not in weather conditions where visibility is bad.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So with knowledge of how fast falcons fly, bird stations in northern Australia can notify wind farms further south of the Falcons approach so that turbines can be shut down as they pass by.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Then another piece of research was done a couple of years later by Conway in 2006.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: His team detected the calling frequency of seabirds flying at night.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Acoustic signals are important communication tools for birds.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: These signals can indicate social cohesion, prey, location and breeding behaviour.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Courtship songs are common amongst various species during mating seasons.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Males produce calling songs that attract distant females, and then courtship songs will induce nearby females to respond.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Surveyors also took recordings of the sounds of all the individual birds detected.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A tablet PC was used to process detailed information like sound pitch, spectrum, length and timing of surveys to minimise the disturbance on the bird community.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: All the sounds were recorded from a distance, using microphones to detect noise.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: They found that the probability of call events was much higher for solitary birds communicating early and late in the day.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Further analysis indicated that during foraging, the frequency of calls was significantly greater for birds encountering schooling, fish and birds called sooner after a catch in these foraging scenarios compared with when only single fish were encountered.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The results of this study showed that increased calling activity in the presence of more profitable prey could be of crucial importance to seabirds that benefit from group foraging.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So does anyone have more questions on?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: That is the end of part four.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: You now have one minute to check your answers to part four.

segments.text: Test for this is the Isles listening test.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: 1 to 6.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Hello.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Oh, hello.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I wanted to inquire about the house you're going to let out.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Is it still available?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: May I ask where you heard about it?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Was it in an advert?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Right, it was.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: What do you want to know?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Well, I'm going to share the house with two friends.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We've been staying on campus, but we're going to graduate, so we need to find a house as soon as possible anyway.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Could you tell me the exact date when you can move in?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Well, the contract with my current tenant is due next week on May the third, and I need a day to clean and check the things in the house.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I think the house will be ready on the 5th of May.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Is that okay?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yes, that will be fine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And what we're most concerned about is the rent.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We'd like something around $500 a month for each of us.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But we could go up to $600 if we have to.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But we can't go beyond that.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You are lucky.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The rent will be 1700 dollars in total, which is within your budget.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: You'll need to pay monthly to me by cash or credit card.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I don't mind.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And you'll have to pay me $500 as a deposit before you move in.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The deposit is as insurance in case you break something.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Okay, that's reasonable.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Oh, I nearly forgot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: One important thing is that you'll be required to provide a credit check to guarantee your ability to pay the rent every month.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This will charge you $15.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: No problem.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How about the facilities?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: First, there are three bedrooms combined with two bathrooms.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Then there is a shared kitchen which was refurbished several months ago.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: By the way, do you cook yourselves?

segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We like cooking.

segments.text: Do we have to buy our own cookers?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Basic facilities for cooking are available, but if you want a dishwasher.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I'm sorry.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It needs to be added later.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I think the basic facilities are enough for us.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Is there any place we can park?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: As one of my friends has a private car.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yes, there is a garage which not only provides space for your car, but also has a special section where you can do some of your work.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's very quiet for you to concentrate.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It sounds so special.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now listen and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There are some other utilities.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I have to tell you.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There is a garden in front of the house in which you will find some interesting plants and beautiful flowers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Do we have to take care of these plants and flowers?

segments.text: Well, you don't have to worry about that.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There will be a professional gardener to do the landscaping in the garden regularly.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: But you do need to help water the grass once a week.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
