segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You now have one minute to check your answers to part one. ------------------------------------------------------- Part two, you will hear an audio guide to the State Museum and its exhibitions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Welcome to the State Museum.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Situated in the center of this truly multi-cultural metropolis, which is home to more than 30 different nationalities.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The museum has a number of exciting displays and exhibitions, and this audio guide is designed to help you fully enjoy your visit.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There are 15 galleries in total and this season sees the opening of three new exhibitions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: We suggest that you start your tour with these highlights of the season.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The Heritage Clothes exhibition is located in Gallery three of the museum.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: People who live in the area have spent two years preparing this exhibition, which brings together some of the fascinating garments traditionally worn in their own communities.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: They looked into the history of their communities, clothing, traditions, and the customs and rituals related to them.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Overall, there are six countries from five continents being represented.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The photos that accompany each exhibit were taken by some of the city's college students who are studying design and show the clothes being modeled by the real people who wear them in the course of their everyday lives.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Another remarkable highlight of the season is the exhibition known as Toys from the Past, which can be visited in Gallery nine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This exhibition, appealing to people of all ages, is on tour throughout the country and will be here for ten weeks only.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Items on display include dolls produced over a century ago with beautiful porcelain faces and in some cases, real hair.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The whole collection covers antique toys, such as wooden train sets from many different generations and offers plenty of fun to children and adults.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The gigantic board games laid out on the gallery floor are among the most popular activities in the exhibition and should not be missed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A special display of miniature toys brings this exhibition to an end.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: These small objects are on loan from countries all over the world, some of which measure no more than a few centimeters.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There is a tiny car made from matchsticks, a toy airplane with the pilot and passengers made out of seashells and some delicate mini houses.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: No higher than four centimeters.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now listen and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The final highlight of the season is the Biscuits Gallery number 15.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: About two decades ago, this city was renowned for its biscuits.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Although today, the factory no longer exists.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Did you know, for example, that before biscuits were wrapped in paper or cardboard boxes, biscuit tins were fashioned items.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The factory manufactured round, square, triangular and hexagonal tins for a whole range of different occasions to celebrate national events, festivals, famous faces, etc..

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: One fascinating exhibition displays people's favorite biscuits.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There are sweet biscuits and savory ones, biscuits filled with jam and biscuits filled with currants, biscuits with colored toppings from sugar icing to chocolate sprinkles.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: When the factory finally closed, it announced that people's favorite biscuit was not, as you might expect, a chocolate biscuit or one filled with jam and cream, but a plain savory one which was eaten with cheese.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: When you get to the end of the exhibition, there is an entertaining hands on activity to fill your own biscuit tin.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: All the biscuits ever produced by the company are piled up on the table along with various tins.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: These biscuit replicas are made out of thin pieces of wood, but the weight, colors and shapes highly resemble the original biscuits.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Your job is to fill the tin with biscuits, and when the lid is taken off, the biscuits are neatly placed as if the job were performed by a machine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It may not be as easy as it seems.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: If you would like to buy a memento of your visit.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There is a museum gift shop which sells postcards, souvenirs and handmade pottery next to the information desk on the ground floor.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And finally, if you don't want to carry your coats and bags around with you during your visit, please make use of the complimentary lockers provided by the museum.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Enjoy your visit.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That is the end of part two.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two. ------------------------------------------------------------- Part four, you will hear part of a lecture on cube houses in Rotterdam.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Good morning.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: In today's lecture, we're going to look at the cube houses, an iconic architectural complex in Rotterdam.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: First, I'm going to be telling you about the history behind it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: As many may know, not much survived the bombing of Rotterdam during World War Two, and it took a long while for the city to start the urban regeneration project.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Dutch architect Blom designed Rotterdam's Cube houses in the late seventies at the request of the city's planners.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: He had previously experimented with cubic architecture in the city of Helmond, so when he was offered this project in the older half an area of the city, he decided to expand upon his original idea.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Blom believed that urban communities should live together under an urban roof.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: He designed the cube houses to recreate daily life in a village where individuals are closely connected and yet have their own separate space.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And even after more than 30 years, the cube houses remain one of the city's most eye catching developments.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Is easy to see why these striking homes are cubes tilted 45 degrees on their side.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The result is buildings that look, feel and behave unlike anything you'll find elsewhere in the world.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The concept behind these houses is that each elevated cube seems like a tree.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And collectively, the cube houses are in the shape of a forest with each triangular roof representing a treetop.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Interestingly, these houses are located right over a pedestrian bridge across one of the busiest streets into the city center next to a railway station.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The traffic free area that connects the cubes includes a little children's playground, as well as small offices and studios with thriving restaurants and cafes right on the doorstep that were designed with the community very much in mind.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: However, the Cube housing development endured various challenges and complications during design and construction, and it once stopped as the designer had difficulty in finance.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Luckily, the project resumed within two weeks after the designer received another round of grants from the City Council.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So what makes the cube houses different from traditional architecture?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Let's look at some of its unique design features.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Each Cube house has a space of 100 square meters and is divided into three floors, and it is very striking to see these houses fixed on one angle.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The tilted residences are constructed on three concrete pillars.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The whole construction is made of 38 regular cube units, all connected together with two super sized cubes at both ends of the string.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: One of the two larger cubes was developed as an architecture school and there is another building recently built between it and a warehouse.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Standing at three floors tall.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Their ground floor is the entrance.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: When you enter a cube house, the first thing to get used to is that all the walls are slanted.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You must take a narrow staircase to reach the lower floor.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This level and the top level are both triangle shaped.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The lower level contains an open kitchen and a living room.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The medium level house is a bathroom and two bedrooms, while the top level provides a great view.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Since the apex of the room is a three sided pyramid with windows all around.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: In some cases, the top floor is used as a small rooftop garden, and as you enter the top half of the structure, your initial inclination may well be to mind your head.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now that you know the history and design features behind these odd looking houses, you might be thinking about how it is to live in them.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: After curious bystanders kept disturbing the cube houses residents.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: One shrewd owner opened the show Cube Museum, which gives visitors the chance to take a tour around a fully furnished Cube house.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It also highlights some of the everyday challenges that the residents face, such as buying and fitting furniture for a structure without straight walls.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: In recent years, Rotterdam's Cube houses have been joined by another architectural icon just across the square.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Rotterdam's Market Hall, the largest indoor market in the Netherlands, is another multi-purpose, residential and retail complex that will live long in your memory, as well as helping to fill your belly with tasty treats.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: In 2009, the Rotterdam based personal architecture BNA converted one of the larger cubes for one of the leading stock hostel chains in the Netherlands.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Today, the hostel invites everyone to experience what it's like to live in a cube house and enjoy a stunning panoramic vista of the surrounding area.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: What attracts guests most is its ideal location, with a major railway station within a five minute walk.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The accommodation is also offered at a fair price, which appeals to visitors both from home and abroad.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That is the end of part four.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You now have one minute to check your answers to part four. ----------------------------------------------------------- Part three, you will hear two students called Jeanie and Dan discussing some research on the effects of music on consumer behavior.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Hi, Dan.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How's it going?

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Hello, Jeanie.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Pretty well, thanks.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Have you finished your research yet?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yes, it's all done.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I've spent several weeks on it from the very beginning of deciding the topic to carrying out the research and writing the essay.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Congratulations.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Seems like a big project.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I know the research is to do with music, but what is it exactly about?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Well, at first I didn't have a specific purpose until one day I read a report that said, if appropriate music is played while people are eating, it may cause some changes in their behavior.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But the report didn't illustrate the changes in detail.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So I wanted to carry out a thorough investigation into this.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That's quite unique.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So how did you conduct your research?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I started by looking for five different restaurants and then went to each of the restaurants to order some food and observe other people.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I mainly focused on how the music is played instead of how people eat.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Findings of my observations indicate that the five restaurants have something in common.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: They all have a special section to play the music.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: More importantly, although the music is played at different times, the volume is unchanged.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: This sounds attractive.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I've never read anything about this before.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: In addition to observation, what other research methods have you used?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I also distributed the survey questionnaire to people dining there.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: What questions are posing your questionnaire?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Well, the first section of the questionnaire asks subjects to indicate the number of times they have been to the restaurant previously, the number of people they dine with, and whether they think they will return to the restaurant.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: These early questions don't involve musical preferences, but largely act as distracted as the intention being that subjects will be less inclined to think that the survey is about the music being played.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: That sounds very reasonable.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Did you design the questionnaire by yourself?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Actually, no.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I read an assignment a student wrote last year, which was just kept beside a dictionary in the library.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I came across it when I was looking something up in the dictionary.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Oh, you're so lucky.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Is there any other question included in the questionnaire?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Subjects are also asked why they choose to dine at a particular restaurant.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Several reasons are listed in the questionnaire.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I thought people would put service first, but that's not the case.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Only about 12% of them have chosen this reason.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: While the majority of respondents think whether they will pick this restaurant depends on how many available seats it has.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: They think it's terrible to eat in a crowded place.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yes, everyone wants to enjoy a meal comfortably.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Then I guess maybe the location of a restaurant is an important factor, since no one likes to waste too much time on the way.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It used to be.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But nowadays, nearly every household has a private car, so they don't have to be worried about the traffic problem.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: What I find interesting, however, is that a large percentage of people say they will compare different restaurants in the neighborhood on the Internet first.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: If one of them stands out from its rivals, they will choose it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Wow.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: It's really interesting.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Before you head the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now listen and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: What else?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Well, the second section of the questionnaire asks subjects to respond to the music being played by rating so that the relationship between music and perceived atmosphere could be examined directly as a means of examining purchase intention.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The final section of the questionnaire asks them to indicate the maximum amount of money they are prepared to spend on their main meal.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So what have you finally discovered?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I collected all the questionnaires and analyzed people's answers to get a clear idea of their reactions to different music conditions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The result shows that music has become an indispensable part of restaurants.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: If people find there isn't any music during the meal, they will think the restaurant charge is too much.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Yes, now music is everywhere in our life.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Is there any difference in people's attitudes towards different musical styles?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Most people think that if jazz is being played when eating, they tend to stay at the restaurant longer and order more food to enjoy the music.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1

segments.transcript: In today's lecture, we're going to look at the cube houses, an iconic architectural complex in Rotterdam.

segments.transcript: First, I'm going to be telling you about the history behind it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: As many may know, not much survived the bombing of Rotterdam during World War Two, and it took a long while for the city to start the urban regeneration project.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Dutch architect Blom designed Rotterdam's Cube houses in the late seventies at the request of the city's planners.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: He had previously experimented with cubic architecture in the city of Helmond, so when he was offered this project in the older half an area of the city, he decided to expand upon his original idea.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Blom believed that urban communities should live together under an urban roof.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: He designed the cube houses to recreate daily life in a village where individuals are closely connected and yet have their own separate space.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: And even after more than 30 years, the cube houses remain one of the city's most eye catching developments.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Is easy to see why these striking homes are cubes tilted 45 degrees on their side.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The result is buildings that look, feel and behave unlike anything you'll find elsewhere in the world.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The concept behind these houses is that each elevated cube seems like a tree.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: And collectively, the cube houses are in the shape of a forest with each triangular roof representing a treetop.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Interestingly, these houses are located right over a pedestrian bridge across one of the busiest streets into the city center next to a railway station.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The traffic free area that connects the cubes includes a little children's playground, as well as small offices and studios with thriving restaurants and cafes right on the doorstep that were designed with the community very much in mind.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: However, the Cube housing development endured various challenges and complications during design and construction, and it once stopped as the designer had difficulty in finance.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Luckily, the project resumed within two weeks after the designer received another round of grants from the City Council.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: So what makes the cube houses different from traditional architecture?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Let's look at some of its unique design features.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: Each Cube house has a space of 100 square meters and is divided into three floors, and it is very striking to see these houses fixed on one angle.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The tilted residences are constructed on three concrete pillars.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: The whole construction is made of 38 regular cube units, all connected together with two super sized cubes at both ends of the string.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: One of the two larger cubes was developed as an architecture school and there is another building recently built between it and a warehouse.

segments.transcript: Standing at three floors tall.

segments.text: Part two, you will hear a tour guide from Travel Light Travel Agency giving some information about a trip to Southern Scotland.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Part four, you will hear part of a lecture on learner persistence.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: First, you have some time to look at questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Today I'm going to talk about my research on learner persistence.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Let me first introduce why I wanted to carry out such research.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: As a university teacher, I found learners responses to certain things vary a lot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: For example, some students may completely give up their degree studies because of a temporary illness, while others may overcome all kinds of difficulties and try their best to continue their studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The latter are the students with learner persistence, and this is the group that I'm particularly interested in to do the research.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: First, I selected my undergraduate students as the research sample with a total of 200 people.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: All the students selected were seniors and they had already stayed in the course very well, although the sample was drawn from a range of ages.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There were deliberately a large number of mature students, and there was one thing in common all of those students were living at home in the local region.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I wanted to maintain this element of consistency, so I didn't include those coming from outside this area.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Then I designed a questionnaire that aimed to find out what their concerns had been when they began the course and then what had made them stick to the three year studies in university.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Findings from the first section pointed out that there were different concerns when they started their university studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: For example, some worried about the financial circumstances, while others were concerned about their careers after graduation.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: However, the research found the biggest concern for mature students tended to be the relationship with their children at home.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Next, I wanted to find out what had made those students persist with their university studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So in the second part, I designed my questionnaire and the three main headings social and environmental factors, other factors and personal characteristics, and I included three levels of importance for each of these three headings.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: At the first level, those points identified by the respondents were regarded as the most important in learner persistence.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Let's look at them one by one for the first column.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: That's the social and environmental factors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A significant number of students said it was crucial to have effective support, whether from their tutors or friends.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: For other factors, students were driven not so much by high grades, but by what they regarded as a success in their studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This was quite different from what I'd expected regarding personal characteristics.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A sizable percentage of participants said they'd like to take up a challenge, which was seen as a very important factor.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Then at the second level of importance in the first category, many of the respondents regarded the life they enjoyed at school as an important social factor because this gave them good experiences.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In the second column, other factors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A lot of people said that the most significant thing was decent health, which was also conducive to their persistence in the studies and then under the third column.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Quite a number of respondents had the same view that they should have a range of interests in their everyday lives because this could broaden their minds and give them a sense of perspective which less persistent learners might lack.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And then onto the third level of importance under social factors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Several respondents said that they had been keeping close to their tutors in their three year university studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In the second column, for other factors, they mentioned it was very important to live in a family without any problems.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And finally, under column three, they talked about the capacity for multi-tasking, which was the ability to simultaneously deal with different problems.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: From these findings, I've concluded some recommendations on how to promote students learner persistence.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Primarily, I suggest that we should distribute questionnaires to the freshmen so as to make clear of their maturity when they begin the course.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: This is really our most important concern.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Secondly, I propose that we should find ways to offer some training sessions to the students who are selected to encourage them to play the role of advisors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The purpose of this is to make support much more approachable to other students.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Thirdly, in the evening and night when offices are closed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Students may have no one to turn to for help.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: As a result, I think we should provide online services to those in need.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Researchers have pointed out that this service is actually more accessible than traditional services.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And finally, if students don't submit their assignments before the deadlines, I think we teachers should contact the students first rather than waiting for the students to come to us.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So this is all I want to share on my research.

segments.transcript: For example, some students may completely give up their degree studies because of a temporary illness, while others may overcome all kinds of difficulties and try their best to continue their studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The latter are the students with learner persistence, and this is the group that I'm particularly interested in to do the research.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: First, I selected my undergraduate students as the research sample with a total of 200 people.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: All the students selected were seniors and they had already stayed in the course very well, although the sample was drawn from a range of ages.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: There were deliberately a large number of mature students, and there was one thing in common all of those students were living at home in the local region.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: I wanted to maintain this element of consistency, so I didn't include those coming from outside this area.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Then I designed a questionnaire that aimed to find out what their concerns had been when they began the course and then what had made them stick to the three year studies in university.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Findings from the first section pointed out that there were different concerns when they started their university studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: For example, some worried about the financial circumstances, while others were concerned about their careers after graduation.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: However, the research found the biggest concern for mature students tended to be the relationship with their children at home.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Next, I wanted to find out what had made those students persist with their university studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So in the second part, I designed my questionnaire and the three main headings social and environmental factors, other factors and personal characteristics, and I included three levels of importance for each of these three headings.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: At the first level, those points identified by the respondents were regarded as the most important in learner persistence.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Let's look at them one by one for the first column.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: That's the social and environmental factors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A significant number of students said it was crucial to have effective support, whether from their tutors or friends.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: For other factors, students were driven not so much by high grades, but by what they regarded as a success in their studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: This was quite different from what I'd expected regarding personal characteristics.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A sizable percentage of participants said they'd like to take up a challenge, which was seen as a very important factor.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Then at the second level of importance in the first category, many of the respondents regarded the life they enjoyed at school as an important social factor because this gave them good experiences.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: In the second column, other factors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: A lot of people said that the most significant thing was decent health, which was also conducive to their persistence in the studies and then under the third column.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Quite a number of respondents had the same view that they should have a range of interests in their everyday lives because this could broaden their minds and give them a sense of perspective which less persistent learners might lack.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: And then onto the third level of importance under social factors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Several respondents said that they had been keeping close to their tutors in their three year university studies.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: In the second column, for other factors, they mentioned it was very important to live in a family without any problems.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: And finally, under column three, they talked about the capacity for multi-tasking, which was the ability to simultaneously deal with different problems.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: From these findings, I've concluded some recommendations on how to promote students learner persistence.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Primarily, I suggest that we should distribute questionnaires to the freshmen so as to make clear of their maturity when they begin the course.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: This is really our most important concern.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Secondly, I propose that we should find ways to offer some training sessions to the students who are selected to encourage them to play the role of advisors.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: The purpose of this is to make support much more approachable to other students.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Thirdly, in the evening and night when offices are closed.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Students may have no one to turn to for help.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: As a result, I think we should provide online services to those in need.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Researchers have pointed out that this service is actually more accessible than traditional services.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: And finally, if students don't submit their assignments before the deadlines, I think we teachers should contact the students first rather than waiting for the students to come to us.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: So this is all I want to share on my research.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Now let's turn to the next part.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.transcript: Are there any questions about.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.transcript: That is the end of part four.
